key_idea: Split the edges into those with a<b and those with a>b: each class is acyclic by itself, and the larger one has at least m/2 edges, so the answer is always YES.
sketch: Edges going from a smaller to a larger label respect the identity order, so they can never form a cycle; the same holds for the decreasing edges with the reversed order. Output the larger class with its 1-based indices. O(m). Multiple answers are valid; the output is acyclic by construction and of size >= ceil(m/2), and it happened to match all three sample outputs exactly. Pitfall: NO never occurs, and duplicate edges are simply kept.
